title: Metabolic efficiency and amino acid composition in the proteomes of Escherichia coli and Bacillus subtilis
one_line_finding: Founding paper of amino-acid biosynthetic cost; shows highly expressed proteins are enriched in metabolically cheap residues - establishes the cost-per-residue concept the index reuses.

title: Energy constraints on the evolution of gene expression
one_line_finding: Wagner computes the whole-cell ATP cost of expressing a gene in yeast (transcription + translation + precursors); the per-protein ATP accounting is not new.

title: The bioenergetic costs of a gene
one_line_finding: Lynch and Marinov give a general ATP-per-gene cost framework across bacteria and eukaryotes; sets the baseline that cost accounting is textbook, not novel.

title: Metabolic costs of amino acid and protein production in Escherichia coli
one_line_finding: Kaleta et al. compute ATP cost of each amino acid and of recombinant proteins from glucose, GLYCEROL and acetate using three constraint-based methods - closest methodological precedent for step 1, in E. coli.

title: Evolutionary systems biology of amino acid biosynthetic cost in yeast
one_line_finding: Barton et al. derive amino-acid costs in a yeast genome-scale model and relate them to expression/conservation; yeast-specific cost values already exist.

title: Do amino acid biosynthetic costs constrain protein evolution in Saccharomyces cerevisiae?
one_line_finding: Tests cost-driven selection in yeast proteins; part of the body of work establishing cost-from-composition as a settled method.

title: Amino acid cost and codon-usage biases in 6 prokaryotic genomes
one_line_finding: Links amino-acid cost with codon usage - the joint cost+codon feature view is pre-existing, if in an evolutionary rather than bioprocess frame.

title: Economical evolution: microbes reduce the synthetic cost of extracellular proteins
one_line_finding: Shows SECRETED proteins are specifically built from cheap amino acids - directly relevant prior framing of secretion cost from composition.

title: COBRAme: a computational framework for genome-scale models of metabolism and gene expression
one_line_finding: ME-model framework (iJL1678b-ME lineage) that already couples translation stoichiometry, ATP cost and proteome allocation; the state of the art the index is measured against.

title: Reconstruction, simulation and analysis of enzyme-constrained metabolic models using GECKO Toolbox 3.0
one_line_finding: Standard ecModel/GECKO protocol; enzyme-cost constraints for yeasts are off-the-shelf, so adding them is implementation, not novelty.

title: Genome-Scale Modeling of the Protein Secretory Machinery in Yeast
one_line_finding: Feizi et al. PSIM: per-protein ATP/GTP/FADH2/GDP-mannose/UDP-GlcNAc/dolichol secretory costs for the whole yeast proteome from exactly signal peptide, N-/O-glyc site counts, disulfide count, GPI, TM, localisation. THE single most dangerous cost prior art. No yield per gram substrate, no titer validation, no recombinant/food proteins.

title: Improving recombinant protein production by yeast through genome-scale modeling using proteome constraints
one_line_finding: pcSecYeast: protein-specific secretion reactions from sequence + PTM profile for 8 recombinant proteins (incl. haemoglobin), simulated max production rate, SHAP feature-importance over N-/O-glyc sites, disulfide count, TM and amino-acid composition, and per-protein bottleneck calls (secretory vs metabolic). Closest full-pipeline analogue; S. cerevisiae, pharma proteins, simulated not measured titers.

title: Genome-scale reconstructions of the mammalian secretory pathway predict metabolic costs and limitations of protein secretion
one_line_finding: Gutierrez et al. compute energetic cost and machinery demand of EACH secreted protein, predict metabolic costs and MAXIMUM PRODUCTIVITIES of biotherapeutics, and identify which protein features most affect secretion. Scoops the concept of a cost+feature producibility calculation, in human/mouse/CHO.

title: Inferring secretory and metabolic pathway activity from omic data with secCellFie
one_line_finding: Turns the mammalian secretory reconstruction into a usable scoring tool from omics; shows the field has already productised per-protein secretory scoring.

title: Genome-scale metabolic model of methylotrophic yeast Pichia pastoris and its use for in silico analysis of heterologous protein production
one_line_finding: PpaMBEL1254 with explicit production equations for two recombinant proteins (HSA, hSOD) - per-protein demand reactions in Pichia date to 2010.

title: Model based engineering of Pichia pastoris central metabolism enhances recombinant protein production
one_line_finding: Nocon et al. embed heterologous protein synthesis in a Pichia GEM and predict (and validate) KO/OE targets - the Pichia recombinant-protein FBA template.

title: Genome-scale metabolic model of Pichia pastoris with native and humanized glycosylation of recombinant proteins
one_line_finding: Irani et al. ihGlycopastoris adds native and humanised N-glycosylation to iLC915 and reports BETTER PREDICTION OF PROTEIN YIELD plus glycosylation-type effects on yield; glycan cost in Pichia is already modelled. Could not read full text (paywalled) to confirm whether a g/g substrate ceiling is reported.

title: Comprehensive reconstruction and evaluation of Pichia pastoris genome-scale metabolic model that accounts for 1243 ORFs
one_line_finding: iMT1026 lineage reconstruction; the base model the claim would use.

title: Fine-tuning the P. pastoris iMT1026 genome-scale metabolic model for improved prediction of growth on methanol or glycerol as sole carbon sources
one_line_finding: iMT1026v3 validated specifically on GLYCEROL and METHANOL - the substrate-specific stoichiometry needed for g protein per g substrate already exists and is validated.

title: Curation of Gene-Protein-Reaction Associations Enhances the iPichia Genome-Scale Metabolic Model of Komagataella phaffii
one_line_finding: Current consensus K. phaffii model (iPichia); the live state of the art for the host.

title: Contextualized genome-scale model unveils high-order metabolic effects of the specific growth rate and oxygenation level in recombinant Pichia pastoris
one_line_finding: Condition-contextualised recombinant Pichia GEM; growth-rate/oxygen trade-offs for protein production already mapped.

title: Metabolic modeling to identify engineering targets for Komagataella phaffii: the effect of biomass composition on gene target identification
one_line_finding: Shows predicted targets are sensitive to biomass composition - a direct robustness objection to any single cost number the index reports.

title: Pichia pastoris growth-coupled heme biosynthesis analysis using metabolic modelling
one_line_finding: Pentjuss et al.: iMT1026, X-33 legH strain, glycerol vs methanol, growth-coupled reaction ranking (own algorithm citing Choi 2010, NOT FSEOF). VERIFIED from full text: reports NO maximum theoretical haem or legH yield and NO titer; the only "theoretical maximum" statements concern BIOMASS growth rate on methanol. A 2025 correction exists (Sci Rep 15:33718).

title: Estimation of recombinant protein production in Pichia pastoris based on a constraint-based model
one_line_finding: Tortajada, Llaneras, Ramon, Pico: uses a constraint-based Pichia model + possibilistic MFA to predict ATP flux, then LINEARLY REGRESSES protein productivity on ATP flux with cross-validation. The "regress titer on stoichiometric ATP burden" move is already published - but as a single-strain process soft-sensor, not a cross-protein sequence-informed index. DOI verified via Crossref; abstract read via Semantic Scholar (paywalled at publisher).

title: Genome wide analysis of protein production load in Trichoderma reesei
one_line_finding: First genome-wide stoichiometric model of T. reesei under protein-production conditions; model PREDICTS PROTEIN PRODUCTION RATE and nominates sulphur assimilation as the limit. The T. reesei half of the cost claim is substantially pre-existing.

title: Whole-genome metabolic model of Trichoderma reesei built by comparative reconstruction
one_line_finding: The T. reesei GEM itself.

title: Predicting Protein Producibility In Filamentous Fungi
one_line_finding: Dykstra, Rousu, Arvas: supervised/semi-supervised SVMs predict RECOMBINANT PROTEIN PRODUCIBILITY in T. reesei and A. niger from sequence (amino-acid composition + Pfam domains), with cross-species transfer tests. The exact term "producibility", the exact host, and the sequence-ML approach are already published. Preprint only; bioRxiv API reports published = NA, i.e. no journal version found.

title: Machine Learning of Protein Interactions in Fungal Secretory Pathways
one_line_finding: Same group applying ML to fungal secretion; reinforces that fungal secretion ML is an established line.

title: Massively parallel interrogation of protein fragment secretability using SECRiFY reveals features influencing secretory system transit
one_line_finding: Experimentally measures secretability of >100,000 fragments in S. cerevisiae AND P. PASTORIS and learns sequence determinants, finding INTRINSIC DISORDER and chain flexibility dominant. Pre-empts the "disorder as a secretion feature" element, with real data rather than literature titers.

title: Evolutionary adaptation of the protein folding pathway for secretability
one_line_finding: Sequence/folding determinants of secretability; the feature-to-secretion mapping literature is mature.

title: Predicting the expression of recombinant monoclonal antibodies in Chinese hamster ovary cells based on sequence features of the CDR3 domain
one_line_finding: Builds a model predicting MEASURED titer from protein coding sequence features across a panel of products - the canonical "sequence features -> titer regression" precedent the claim must be distinguished from.

title: Developability index: a rapid in silico tool for the screening of antibody aggregation propensity
one_line_finding: The original single-number sequence/structure-derived "index" for manufacturability; establishes that composite producibility indices are an accepted, long-standing device.

title: Protein-Sol: a web tool for predicting protein solubility from sequence
one_line_finding: Sequence-only solubility predictor; one of the off-the-shelf feature generators.

title: SoluProt: prediction of soluble protein expression in Escherichia coli
one_line_finding: Predicts SOLUBLE EXPRESSION (not just solubility) from sequence; same conceptual target as a producibility score, in E. coli.

title: ccSOL omics: a webserver for solubility prediction of endogenous and heterologous expression in Escherichia coli
one_line_finding: Proteome-scale heterologous-expression solubility scoring; precedent for scoring whole panels.

title: Prediction of protein solubility based on sequence physicochemical patterns and distributed representation information with DeepSoluE
one_line_finding: Current deep-learning solubility predictor.

title: SignalP 5.0 improves signal peptide predictions using deep neural networks
one_line_finding: Signal-peptide prediction component of the feature panel.

title: SignalP 6.0 achieves signal peptide prediction across all types using protein language models
one_line_finding: SignalP 6.0 preprint record (journal version in Nat Biotechnol 2022 not verified in this audit).

title: Toward Rational Design of Precision-Fermented Milk Proteins: Integrating Cross-Species Selection, Post-Translational Modification, and AI Optimization
journal: Compr Rev Food Sci Food Saf
one_line_finding: Already publishes the QUALITATIVE ANSWER the index is meant to produce: alpha-lactalbumin and beta-lactoglobulin most tractable (minimal PTM dependency), caseins and lactoferrin hardest (phosphorylation/glycosylation unavailable in microbial hosts). Biggest threat to the index's conclusions, not its method.

title: Methylotrophic yeast engineering for secreted protein production via precision fermentation: food ingredient proteins and synthetic biology strategies
one_line_finding: Reviews K. phaffii food-protein production with explicit attention to secretion efficiency, space-time yield and PTM fidelity; the qualitative landscape is covered.

title: Harnessing Fungal Secretion Systems for Precision Fermentation of Food Proteins
one_line_finding: Perspective arguing food-protein viability hinges on gram-per-litre secretion and cost; frames the problem the index addresses but offers no quantitative per-protein score.

title: The Next Food Revolution Is Here: Recombinant Microbial Production of Milk and Egg Proteins by Precision Fermentation
one_line_finding: Anchor review of the field; host/protein/regulatory landscape.

title: Production of bovine beta-lactoglobulin and hen egg ovalbumin by Trichoderma reesei using precision fermentation technology and testing of their techno-functional properties
one_line_finding: Peer-reviewed T. reesei benchmark titers for BLG and ovalbumin; a training point for any titer regression.

title: High-level secretory production of leghemoglobin in Pichia pastoris through enhanced globin expression and heme biosynthesis
one_line_finding: Highest reported secreted LegH titer in K. phaffii; the leghemoglobin training point.

title: Precision fermentation of kappa-casein using Pichia pastoris
one_line_finding: Recent casein-in-Pichia production paper; casein training point and evidence the hardest target is now being attempted.

title: Ovalbumin production using Trichoderma reesei culture and low-carbon energy could mitigate the environmental impacts of chicken-egg-derived ovalbumin
one_line_finding: LCA, not stoichiometric cost; shows the environmental side is done but the per-protein metabolic ceiling is not its object.

title: Scale-up economics for cultured meat
one_line_finding: Humbird's transparent bottom-up bioprocess cost model built on stoichiometric substrate-to-product yields; the TEA machinery exists and should be reused, not re-derived.

title: Minimum viable products in precision fermentation: defining translational milestones for food biotechnology
one_line_finding: Current framing of economic milestones for precision-fermented foods.

title: Deletion of low-essentiality, secretion-associated genes enhances recombinant protein production in Komagataella phaffii
one_line_finding: Same group as the unpublished Acharya K. phaffii GEM bottleneck manuscript; indicates an active, well-resourced competitor on exactly this host.

title: Genome-Scale Metabolic Models Identify Metabolic Bottlenecks in Production of Recombinant Proteins in Komagataella phaffii (Acharya et al., manuscript; code at github.com/RaghavAcharya/kphaffii-metabolic-bottlenecks)
one_line_finding: NO DOI FOUND - not in Europe PMC or Crossref as of this audit; only the public code repo (last push 2026-10-29). README documents iMT1026v3 adapted to four recombinant proteins (VHH, RBD, HSA, IgG1) with custom builders for translation, N-/O-glycosylation, disulfide, COPII and PTMs, a PSIM-style per-gene property table (sequence, localisation, PTM counts, signal-peptide/GPI/TM flags), FSEOF target identification and a PER-GENE/PER-PROTEIN NUTRIENT COST pipeline. The sharpest live scoop risk for steps 1-2 in exactly this host.
